description: Open-source 3D anatomy explorer: 2,234 selectable BodyParts3D meshes, system layers, search, and exploded views.

summary.one_liner: An open-source interactive 3D human anatomy explorer built with React and Three.js, letting users select, search, and isolate 2,234 individual body-structure meshes from the BodyParts3D reference model.
summary.what_it_does: The app loads the BodyParts3D 4.0 adult male reference anatomy and splits it into 2,234 individually selectable meshes. Users can orbit, zoom, and click structures on the body, and toggle 15 anatomical systems or use skeleton and organ presets. A search covers 3,432 named concepts and source identifiers. Selecting a structure isolates it and shows its details, and an exploded view spreads all visible pieces into a spaced inventory. The README says the interface has been tested at phone and tablet sizes, with tap-versus-drag handling. It also describes optional WebMCP tools for search and inspection in compatible browsers.
use_cases: searching for a named anatomical structure
isolating and reading about a single organ
creating exploded views of anatomy for teaching
viewing anatomy on a phone or tablet
how_to_run: Open the local dev server URL in a browser
npm run build (static output goes to dist/)
notable: Splits the BodyParts3D adult male model into 2,234 individually selectable meshes
Covers 15 anatomical systems and 3,432 named concepts with search
Exploded layout packs only visible pieces into a non-overlapping inventory
Batched geometry with GPU textures for translation, visibility, and selection
Runs without API keys or accounts; deployable as a static site (Vercel config included)
caveats: Anatomy data is a single adult male reference and does not represent every human structure or variation
Explicitly educational, not a diagnostic or surgical tool
Physical-device performance and real multitouch hardware were not tested, per the README
Packaged model is roughly 33 MB of compressed geometry and 2.3M triangles, so initial load can be heavy
